## TL;DR

RepoOS Hub’s Capacitor shell (`mobile/`) now matches the web app’s design themes and light/dark/system modes, with a dedicated Settings page, redesigned server list, Lucide icons, and platform-aware styling. Browser `?fixture=` seeds support dev review; unit tests cover theme/mode persistence, list states, settings navigation, and how shot resolution should work once `repoos-mobile-dev` exists. On-device flash-free boot, store builds, and Hub screenshots on the mobile preview remain follow-ups — including Nick adding the preview target to `repoos.toml` on main.

## Work and rationale

The old shell inlined device lock, used text-arrow reorder controls, and stayed on one dark palette. This branch keeps the shell a thin picker (ADR 0011): list, lock, settings, add/edit, and isolated WebView open — no board UI in Capacitor.

Themes reuse `mobile/src/design-tokens` and generated `ui-themes.css` (`sync-ui-theme-vars.mjs`). `theme-core.ts` holds pure DOM/keys logic for tests in the main repo; Capacitor Preferences live in `theme.ts`. `mobile/index.html` applies saved theme/mode (and shot query overrides) before Vue paints in the browser harness.

Navigation is picker → settings → add, with edit/delete in a bottom sheet. `ServerListView` delivers cards, reachability, empty state, and edit-mode drag. `fixture.ts` drives list/settings routes only on the Vite dev server via `?fixture=`.

`src/core/shot-page.ts` screenshots the first match when a selector hits multiple `#app` nodes (main app mount + root). `## Shots` stays empty until the mobile preview target is on the board config — Hub routes must not aim at `default`.

## Approaches tried

- Module state in `app-state.ts` instead of Pinia for four screens.
- Theme sync script from `src/ui-app` CSS instead of hand-copied palettes.
- Edit-mode reorder vs always-visible arrows for touch UX.
- Table-driven fixture/theme tests in `mobile-hub-shell.test.ts` rather than mounting Hub SFCs through ui-app’s vitest root (avoids Capacitor in the main gate).
- Cleared mistaken Hub shots on `default`; evidence waits on `repoos-mobile-dev`.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Preview target not on main:** `repoos update --shots` validates target names against the main checkout’s `repoos.toml`, which still has only `default`, Landing, and Docs. **`[[preview.targets]]` `repoos-mobile-dev` must be added by Nick on main** (see snippet below) before declared Hub shots can validate and handoff capture can boot the mobile Vite app. This task branch intentionally does not change `repoos.toml`.
- **`needs_input` / on-device AC:** Flash-free Preferences boot and hardware polish need a real device (already flagged on the task).
- **`just build-android`:** Not run in this pass; depends on local SDK.
- **`repoos.toml` close-out:** When Nick lands the preview row, merge/conflict rules apply; mobile tasks should declare that path in task metadata if required by RepoOS guards.

Recommended row for Nick on `main` `repoos.toml` (after Docs site target):

```toml
[[preview.targets]]
name = "repoos-mobile-dev"
areas = ["mobile"]
paths = ["mobile/**"]
command = "bun run dev -- --port {port} --host {host} --strictPort"
cwd = "mobile"
readyPath = "/"
```

Then re-declare 390×844 Hub shots with `"target": "repoos-mobile-dev"`.

## Key learnings

- Mobile Hub UI must not use `default` preview or Mission Control will render instead of the picker.
- `theme-core.ts` keeps Capacitor out of the main test typecheck path.
- Dev fixtures stay query-param only; production uses real Preferences storage.
- Engineering report + empty shots is the right handoff when preview registration is human-owned config.
